title: 90-Day Window Opens for Foreign Traders to Regularise in Kenya
desc: Foreign traders in Kenya have 90 days to regularise immigration, business and work documents before stricter enforcement begins.
content:
Foreign nationals operating businesses in Kenya have been given 90 days to regularise their immigration and business status, as the government moves to enforce existing rules governing foreign participation in local trade.

The directive was announced by State House on Tuesday, September 8, 2026, following growing concerns over foreign nationals operating businesses in areas traditionally dominated by Kenyan traders. The regularisation period is intended to give affected traders time to ensure their documentation and business operations comply with Kenyan law.

State House spokesperson Hussein Mohamed said the 90-day window will cover the regularisation of relevant requirements, including immigration status, work permits, business registration and operating licences. Traders who fall within the affected categories are expected to use the period to correct any gaps in their documentation.

The announcement comes days after President William Ruto directed authorities to take action against foreign nationals engaging in small-scale trading activities reserved for Kenyan citizens. The government has maintained that foreign investors and traders remain welcome where they operate within the law and in areas permitted to them.

The latest directive therefore shifts the focus from the earlier warning to compliance and enforcement. Rather than immediate action against every affected trader, the government has provided a defined period for those required to regularise their operations.

For Kenyan traders, the move is likely to attract close attention because competition from foreign-owned businesses has been a recurring concern, particularly in informal and small-scale commerce. The government says enforcement is intended to protect opportunities for Kenyan citizens while maintaining a regulated environment for legitimate foreign investment.

For foreign traders, the 90-day period provides an opportunity to establish whether their businesses, immigration status and permits meet the required conditions. Those operating outside the permitted framework could face enforcement once the window expires.

The development also places greater responsibility on government agencies to clearly communicate which businesses and activities are affected and how traders can complete the regularisation process.

With the 90-day deadline for foreign traders in Kenya now announced, attention will shift to how the government implements the directive and whether affected businesses comply before enforcement begins.
